questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The following data are utilized in an experiment to measure the speed of light using Fizeau's apparatus:
Distance between the mirrors $= 12.0 \text{ km}$,
Number of teeth in the wheel $= 180$.
Determine the minimum angular speed of the wheel such that the image is not observed.
questions.solution:
Time taken by light to travel to the mirror and back is $t = \dfrac{2D}{c}$.

For the image to be completely eclipsed (not observed) at the minimum angular speed, the wheel must rotate such that the light passing through a gap is blocked by the adjacent tooth upon its return.

The angle between the center of a gap and the center of the adjacent tooth is $\theta = \dfrac{360^{}^{{}^{\circ}}}{2N}$.

Given $N = 180$, we get $\theta = \dfrac{360^{}^{{}^{\circ}}}{2 \times 180} = 1^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$.

The time taken by the wheel to rotate by this angle is $t = \dfrac{\theta}{\omega}$.

Equating the two expressions for time:

$\dfrac{2D}{c} = \dfrac{\theta}{\omega}$

$\omega = \dfrac{\theta c}{2D}$

Substituting the given values ($D = 12 \times 10^3 \text{ m}$, $c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$, $\theta = 1^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$):

$\omega = \dfrac{1^{}^{{}^{\circ}} \times 3 \times 10^8}{2 \times 12 \times 10^3}$

$\omega = \dfrac{3 \times 10^5}{24} = 12500^{}^{{}^{\circ}}\text{/s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a Michelson experiment intended for measuring the speed of light, the total distance travelled by light between two successive reflections from the rotating mirror is $4.8 \text{ km}$. The rotating mirror is shaped as a regular octagon. Find the minimum non-zero angular speed of the mirror required for the image to be formed at the exact position where a stationary mirror would form it.
questions.solution:
The time taken by light to travel the given distance $D$ is

$t = \dfrac{D}{c} = \dfrac{4.8 \times 10^3}{3 \times 10^8} = 1.6 \times 10^{-5} \text{ s}$

For the image to be formed at the exact position as a stationary mirror, the regular octagonal mirror must rotate by an angle equal to the angle between its adjacent faces in time $t$.

The angle between adjacent faces of a regular octagon is $\dfrac{1}{8}$ of a revolution.

The minimum non-zero angular speed $f$ in revolutions per second is given by

$f = \dfrac{1/8}{t}$

$f = \dfrac{1}{8 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-5}}$

$f = \dfrac{10^5}{12.8} = 7812.5 \text{ rev/s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
For an experiment using Foucault's apparatus, the setup distances are given as follows:
Distance between the rotating and the fixed mirror $= 16 \text{ m}$,
Distance between the lens and the rotating mirror $= 6 \text{ m}$,
Distance between the source and the lens $= 2 \text{ m}$.
Upon rotating the mirror at a speed of $356$ revolutions per second, a shift of $0.7 \text{ mm}$ is observed in the image. Determine the speed of light from this data.
questions.solution:
In Foucault's rotating mirror experiment, the shift in the image is given by the formula:

$s = \dfrac{4 R^2 \omega a}{c (R+b)}$

where:
$R$ = distance between the rotating and fixed mirror = $16 \text{ m}$
$b$ = distance between the lens and the rotating mirror = $6 \text{ m}$
$a$ = distance between the source and the lens = $2 \text{ m}$
$\omega$ = angular velocity of the rotating mirror = $2 \pi n$
$n$ = frequency of rotation = $356 \text{ rev/s}$
$s$ = shift in the image = $0.7 \text{ mm} = 0.7 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$
$c$ = speed of light

Rearranging the formula to solve for the speed of light $c$:

$c = \dfrac{4 R^2 (2 \pi n) a}{s (R+b)}$

Substituting the given values and using $\pi \approx \dfrac{22}{7}$:

$c = \dfrac{8 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 356 \times (16)^2 \times 2}{0.7 \times 10^{-3} \times (16 + 6)}$

$c = \dfrac{8 \times 22 \times 356 \times 256 \times 2}{7 \times 0.7 \times 10^{-3} \times 22}$

Canceling $22$ from the numerator and denominator:

$c = \dfrac{8 \times 356 \times 256 \times 2}{4.9 \times 10^{-3}}$

$c = \dfrac{4096 \times 356}{4.9} \times 10^3$

$c = \dfrac{1458176}{4.9} \times 10^3$

$c \approx 297586 \times 10^3 \text{ m/s}$

$c \approx 2.9758 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$

Rounding to two decimal places, we get $c \approx 2.98 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$.

Answer: $2.98 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$
